narrative:
The model estimated a 56% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, that is slightly above half, so the application was denied rather than approved with conditions.

The strongest reason was the size of the loan you requested: 10,623 DM, far above the approved applicants’ average of about 3,020 DM. A much larger request than typical was the main factor pushing the decision toward bad credit. The second most influential factor was your checking account status: it was overdrawn, a situation seen among only about 12.6% of approved applicants, while most approved applicants had no negative balance. That also pushed toward bad credit. Your credit history was the third most important factor. It showed critical or other credits, and this factor actually worked in your favour, pushing toward good credit, although around one-third of approved applicants share this history. However, that favourable signal was not strong enough to outweigh the concerns about loan size and the overdrawn account.

To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller amount and, if possible, bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying. You could also ask the bank what specific steps would strengthen your credit record, and whether adding a guarantor or co-applicant could support a future application.
